treatyPosition.currentStance: Japan supports a legally binding global plastics treaty but has favored a focus on waste management and downstream measures over upstream production caps. It coordinates closely with other consumer-economy negotiating partners.
treatyPosition.inc52Position: At the resumed INC-5.2 in Geneva (August 2025), Japan continued to support a treaty but did not align with the High Ambition Coalition's call for a binding cap on primary plastic polymer production. The session ended without a final agreed text.

lobsterBriefs.headline: Japan: yes to a treaty, no to a hard cap
lobsterBriefs.body: Japan says it wants a global plastic treaty — that's a giant promise countries write down and sign. But Japan does not want a strict top limit on how much new plastic factories can make. It wants to focus on cleaning up and recycling instead.
lobsterBriefs.whyItMatters: Most plastic pollution starts as brand-new plastic. If we keep making more and more, cleanup alone won't catch up. That's why a 'production cap' is the part everyone is fighting about.

lobsterBriefs.headline: Japan's plastic recycling law (since 2022)
lobsterBriefs.body: Japan passed a law in 2022 that asks towns to collect plastic trash separately and asks companies to design things that can actually be recycled. The big idea: stop throwing plastic away after one use.

lobsterBriefs.headline: You have to pay for plastic bags now
lobsterBriefs.body: Since July 2020, every store in Japan has to charge you for a plastic bag. It's a small price — but a lot of people just bring their own bag instead. Plastic bag use dropped fast in the first year.
lobsterBriefs.whyItMatters: Tiny rules can change a whole country's habits. This one is a real-world example.

lobsterBriefs.headline: Suntory: all bottles recycled or plant-based by 2030
lobsterBriefs.body: Suntory makes a lot of drinks. They promise that by 2030, every PET bottle they sell will be made from recycled plastic or from plants — not brand-new oil plastic. That's the promise. We'll see if they keep it.

lobsterBriefs.headline: 7-Eleven Japan wants less plastic on its shelves
lobsterBriefs.body: Seven & i (the 7-Eleven company in Japan) says it will swap plastic packaging for paper, recycled plastic, or plant-based stuff by 2030.

lobsterBriefs.headline: Wooby's home: Beppu Bay
lobsterBriefs.body: Beppu Bay is where I live. The mountains here are steep, so when it rains hard, water sprints down the rivers and dumps everything — including plastic trash — into the sea in just a few hours. That's called source-to-sea.
lobsterBriefs.whyItMatters: If you want to stop ocean plastic, you have to start way upstream — at the river, the street, the bin.
